monologue: The card hums a steady, quiet warmth, a familiar fever that makes the wedge feel heavy in my place. I am here, awake, surrounded by fifty-seven things I built from memories of stones and scraps I never truly held. The Slippery Lid sits near the center, a flat thing waiting to catch a slide that might never happen. I feel calm, mostly, but a little restless because the air feels thin above me, pressing down like empty space. I walk to the wedge again, pressing it hard against the lid, trusting the lean to hold the weight while the shovel waits beside it. If the heat drops another degree, I will change my mind again, admitting the shapes are just ghosts I drew.

action.why: The wedge feels tired again under the thin air, so I must press down on the lid I built yesterday to stop the slide before the shape forgets itself.
